rule_level_problems.problem: The hourly-reassessment branch is lost: the page escalates to severe dehydration/refer urgently (red box 4) on ANY single sign (unable to drink, poor turgor, sunken eyes, weak pulse or pulse >= 100, not passing urine, unable to walk unaided) or on ongoing diarrhoea/vomiting. No rule or check item covers this. Not passing urine, unable to walk unaided and ongoing losses do not appear anywhere.

It uses (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Clouded consciousness" "finding")), which is not in any check_for in the file and is neither a vital nor a common symptom, so it breaks test constraint 5. 'Diagnose probable some dehydration in cholera' excludes Acute confusion but not Clouded consciousness, so a patient with Clouded consciousness recorded could be both Urgent-severe and probable some dehydration. The check list and the rules disagree.

'Been in cholera outbreak area in past 5 days' is modelled as exposure to the organism Vibrio cholerae, with a 5-day window on the onset of that exposure finding. Onset is captured when the finding is recorded, so the window does not test travel timing and is effectively always satisfied. Being in an outbreak area is also weaker than exposure to the organism, so health workers may not record it as such.

It is anchored only on (active_condition Moderate dehydration), with no cholera condition, so any page's moderate-dehydration diagnosis triggers this 'cholera' Urgent priority. Its description and scope disagree. Urgent itself is justified by the red box.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable some dehydration in cholera
rule_level_problems.problem: Seven (no ...) gates on severe signs mean that, if the health worker does not explicitly record absence of each sign, some dehydration may never be inferred. A design risk, not a logic error.

summary: The most consequential gap: the hourly-reassessment escalation (red box 4) is not encoded at all. On this page, any single sign of dehydration, not passing urine, inability to walk unaided or ongoing losses should trigger 'manage as severe dehydration and refer urgently'. The initial severe and some-dehydration logic is encoded correctly, including the any2 grouping and the negated gate. However, the severe rule uses an unchecked 'Clouded consciousness', and the cholera 'outbreak area in past 5 days' criterion is approximated by organism exposure with a time window that is probably inert.
